title: Replayable session semantics and tool-saga proposal
body:
Context:
This is a working PRD-level proposal for enabling replayable/resumable sessions plus a formal "tool-saga" primitive in the Hosted API. The goal is to make multi-step tool orchestrations (search -> call external API -> commit to database) observable, resumable, and safe for client SDKs to use with streaming incremental outputs and typed payloads.

Why this came up (tl;dr):
- Customers are building long-running assistant flows that call multiple external systems. Failures mid-run leave inconsistent state or force heavy engineering to reconcile.
- Current hosted streaming surface gives tokens/events but lacks a compact model for describing a multi-step transaction with rollback/compensation semantics and deterministic replay for client recovery.
- SDK ergonomics are an open area: we need a pattern that is easy for front-end/back-end libraries to adopt (replay, checkpoint, backpressure, typed tool responses).

Goals:
- Define a wire-level "tool-saga" event envelope that captures ordered tool calls, results, and compensations.
- Provide resume primitives: lightweight checkpoint tokens, idempotency keys, and incremental state diffs so clients can reconnect mid-stream and continue without corrupting external systems.
- Maintain low-latency streaming for progressive user-facing text while separately emitting structured tool events for server-side processing.
- Provide SDK patterns that are simple (1-2 APIs) for common cases and extensible for advanced use.

Non-goals:
- Full orchestration engine (we're not shipping a full long-running workflow runner). This PRD focuses on primitives for clients and hosted API to coordinate with external orchestrators.
- Replacing customer existing sagas/ops frameworks; instead we provide interoperable events and clear idempotency semantics.

User stories:
- As a developer, I want the assistant to call an external payment API and, if the payment fails later in the flow, automatically trigger a compensation call (refund) without double-charging.
- As a platform engineer, I want telemetry that ties tokens/latency to specific tool steps so I can debug slow third-party integrations.
- As an SDK consumer, I want to reconnect after a dropped client network and resume the conversation without re-triggering side-effects.

Key concepts / vocabulary (proposal):
- session_id: a short alphanumeric id assigned at session start (scoped to a conversation).
- checkpoint_token: compact, server-signed token representing last durable event index + minimal state to resume safely.
- tool-call: a request emitted by the LM that intends to invoke an external tool; includes tool_id, call_payload, and call_meta.
- tool-result: structured output from the tool. This is not free-form text but typed JSON schema (optional per tool).
- saga-step: an element in an ordered saga describing forward action and optional compensation action.
- durable-log: an append-only event stream in the control plane that records tool-calls and tool-results for replay/inspection.

Wire format (sketch):
- Streaming response is multiplexed: token-stream frames (for text/assistant tokens) + event frames (json) for tool-saga events.
- Event frame envelope fields (all strings or small maps): {"evt_type": "tool-call|tool-result|checkpoint|saga-finished|saga-aborted", "evt_id": "uuid", "session_id": "S-xxxx", "payload": <stringified JSON>, "index": <monotonic int>}
- Client-side SDK will expose typed callbacks: onToken(token), onEvent(eventEnvelope).

Tool-saga lifecycle example (high level):
1) LM emits tool-call for search (evt_id=e1). Server immediately emits event frame and appends to durable-log.
2) Search tool completes -> server emits tool-result (evt_id=e1-result). result includes matches (typed).
3) LM emits tool-call for charge-card (evt_id=e2). Server emits event frame.
4) Critical: when e2 is sent, server issues a checkpoint_token that indicates the system will consider e2 as "in-flight"; token carries monotonic index 3.
5) If the client disconnects before result, client re-connects with checkpoint_token and receipts; server returns tool-result replay and either continues or triggers compensation depending on policy.

Idempotency and safety model (proposal):
- Each tool-call includes an idempotency_key derived from evt_id and session_id. Providers must accept duplicate submissions and do dedupe based on that key.
- Server will not re-emit forward side-effecting tool-calls automatically on reconnect unless the client explicitly requests "resume-forward" mode. Default behavior: replay results only and let client decide to reissue forward actions.
- Compensation actions can be specified in saga-step metadata: {"compensate_with": "refund_charge", "compensate_on": ["saga-aborted","timeout"]}. The server may surface compensation suggestions but will not run them automatically unless enterprise policy permits.

SDK ergonomics (sketch):
- JS/TS SDK: high-level "session()" builder with fluent handlers:
  const s = client.session({model, session_id});
  s.onToken(t => render(t));
  s.onEvent(e => { if (e.evt_type === 'tool-call') callTool(e); });
  await s.start();

- Resume flow: s.resume({checkpoint_token, resume_mode: 'inspect'|'continue'}).
  - inspect: replay event stream to client but do not re-trigger side effects.
  - continue: attempt to progress LM and optionally re-issue forward tool calls (requires client confirmation by default).

- Backpressure: SDK exposes pauseTokens() / resumeTokens() to signal to runtime. We also expose small consumer-side buffer size config. Server will continue streaming events but will not drop tool events (they are treated as control plane messages).

Structured output and typing:
- Tool results should support an optional schema id. The SDK should validate against schema on receive and surface typed objects to the application (e.g., PaymentResult type).
- For backward compatibility, tools may omit schema; SDK then provides raw string payload and a parsing hook.

Observability + tracing:
- Each event written to durable-log must include trace_id and span_id when available so we can link model latency to tool latencies.
- Expose a per-session timeline view in Console: tokens timeline, tool call ladder, checkpoints, and latencies.
- Add telemetry metric: percent of sessions resumed, number of duplicate idempotent submits, compensation-run counts.

Compatibility with existing Hosted API features:
- Model fallbacks: if the primary model is downgraded mid-saga, the platform must still honor checkpoint semantics and replay tool events to the new model instance.
- Dedicated/Private: checkpoint tokens clearable by customer KMS in Private deployments (privacy/regulatory requirement).

Operational concerns:
- Storage: durable-log retention defaults to 30 days with opt-in longer retention for enterprise. Events are small; estimate ~200KB per long session per hour.
- Security: tool-call payloads may contain PHI/PII — surface per-tool redaction controls and access logging.
- Costs: emitting structured events increases ingress/egress; consider a cost bucket for event retention.

Open questions / trade-offs (we need decisions):
- Should server be permitted to automatically run compensations on abort (safety vs convenience)? (security + billing implications)
- Resume default: inspect (safe) or continue (convenient)? My recommendation: default to inspect; allow clients/apps to opt-in to continue.
- How large should checkpoint_token be? stateless JWT vs opaque server pointer. JWT reduces load but will leak event index logic.
- Do we require idempotency for all tools or provide a shim that stores dedupe state on our side?

Short roadmap / next steps:
- Spike: implement a minimal durable-log + event frames prototype in staging that supports one tool (search) + resume inspect path. (ENG prototype, 3 weeks)
- SDK spike: JS/TS minimal session() wrapper + resume semantics (DEVEX, 2 weeks)
- Security review for token formats and PII handling (SEC, 2 weeks)
- Design: finalize policy for auto-compensations and enterprise controls (PRODUCT, legal)

Notes / TODOs (author):
- Add concrete event envelope schema (json schema) and wire-level encoding for streaming (SSE vs HTTP/2 frames).
- Validate storage sizing with infra (SRE) and include retention pricing in billing doc.
- Add example end-to-end sequence diagram with SDK, control plane, tool runtime, and external tool provider.

References / inspiration:
- Two-phase commit / sagas literature (Microservices sagas)
- Existing partial-response streaming PRDs (see linked artifacts)
- Customer support tickets: CS-3419, CS-3440 (payment retry issues)

Unresolved items for next sync:
- Decide default resume mode and opt-in guardrails.
- Decide whether we implement dedupe shim vs requiring idempotent tool providers.
- Finalize event storage retention and pricing model.
